intro: Lithuania is the largest of the Baltic states, a land of lakes, forests and a spectacular strip of sand dunes on the Baltic coast.

chapters.title: Lakes and dunes
text: Lithuania has thousands of lakes and gentle hills; the highest point is under 300 m. The Nemunas River flows to the Curonian Lagoon, cut off from the sea by the Curonian Spit, a thin strip of tall sand dunes shared with Russia's Kaliningrad region and listed as a World Heritage Site.
Lithuania borders Latvia, Belarus, Poland and Russia. Geographers once calculated that the geographical centre of Europe lies just north of Vilnius.

chapters.title: Climate
text: Lithuania has cold winters and mild summers. Amber, fossilised tree resin, washes up on its beaches after storms.

keyTerms.meaning: A long, narrow strip of sand sticking out into the sea.
